objective: At the owner's request ('Yes, let's continue.', approving NATIVE-GENUS-20261104-001's recommendation): a native reading of the brace tree. Test whether blocks of mutual creation, one-way creation and silence recover a three-fold space's tight-cut decomposition (its Fano atoms, the direction of each cut, its doubled squares), including where atoms touch, and try to prove the block lemma for Fano atoms. No time constraints.
status: Complete 2026-11-05: successful. Native creation reads the brace tree of spaces built from Fano atoms: each atom is a block of mutual creation (proved for atoms attached at a line), every cut between two atoms is read in its direction by one-way creation, and the relation between two atom lines is fixed by the tree wherever only atoms join them (42,090 pairs, no exception). The source rule, fixed from these rules, counts the Heawood braces, and the genus, on all 157 spaces without a non-Fano brace, 110 of them fresh (every three-fold class of 23 to 26 points), where the plain block count fails 32. Refuted: determinism through plane glue, and silence of glue across a Fano atom. Non-Fano handles are not read. Next: a two-bit screening lemma (2/3)
stop_rule: Stop when the block lemma is proved or its unproved part is isolated, when the dictionary between the decomposition and native creation is decided on the census and on trees of atoms, and when a reconstruction fixed in advance has been tested on fresh spaces.
title: A native reading of the brace tree
